features.name: lvnDetection.ts + LVN/HVN eval harness (Phase B)
features.description: Phase B of the LVN/HVN detection effort. lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts: pure, immutable detector over an HTF VbP volume series ({price,volume}[]; no paired delta needed) that returns HVN (high-volume-node peaks) and BOTH LVN types — HVN peaks also feed feat-015 magnetCheck. LVN detection is DUAL-MECHANISM: (a) VALLEY LVNs = local minima between two distributions (prominence/depth detection); (b) TAPER-EDGE LVNs = the shoulder/knee where a distribution tapers into a flat, sustained low-volume plateau (gradient/derivative or relative-threshold-crossing-into-plateau) — a pure local-minima pass MISSES these (e.g. fixture-1 labels 30008/30088 are taper edges, not valleys). Physically meaningful params (neighborhood window, valley/peak prominence/depth threshold, plateau flatness + level for the taper detector); may optionally re-bin a fine (e.g. 1-tick) input series. LVN/HVN output is authoritative and code-owned (no vision round-trip). scripts/lvn-eval.ts (+ npm run lvn:eval): loads each Phase-A fixture + its LVN/HVN labels, greedily matches detected<->labeled levels of the same type by nearest within an ABSOLUTE price tolerance (configurable, default +/-10 points — these are trading levels that align with MGI, NOT bin-relative), computes precision/recall + count delta per type per fixture, prints a per-fixture + aggregate table, reports train vs holdout separately, exits nonzero only when the TRAIN set is below threshold. Colocated unit tests exercise detector mechanics on synthetic series (single valley/peak, flat profile, double distribution, noisy shoulders, AND a taper-edge case: distribution -> low plateau).
features.evidence: lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts: pure, immutable detectLvnHvn(series:{price,volume}[], overrides?) over an HTF VbP volume series (no paired delta). Returns HVN peaks (topographic prominence) + BOTH LVN types — VALLEY (prominence/depth of a trough between distributions) and TAPER-EDGE (relative-threshold-crossing-into-a-flat-low-plateau, gated on a real distribution shoulder just outside the knee) — so a pure local-minima pass no longer misses taper shoulders. Thresholds are RELATIVE (fractions of peak/POC volume) so one param set generalizes across fixtures with 10x-different raw magnitudes; a moving-average smooth de-noises the 1-point bins; output is descending-price to match the export convention. Plain TS types, no Zod, no file I/O (mirrors sibling engine modules). scripts/lvn-eval.ts + `npm run lvn:eval`: loads each Phase-A fixture (loadLvnFixtures, strict) and greedily matches detected<->labeled levels of the same type by nearest within an ABSOLUTE ±10pt tolerance (configurable via --tolerance), computes precision/recall + count-delta per type per fixture, reports TRAIN and HOLDOUT aggregates separately, and exits nonzero only when TRAIN F1 (LVN or HVN) < 0.40 (--threshold, a REGRESSION FLOOR not a quality claim). Detection is code-owned and authoritative — the LLM is NOT asked to confirm/adjust node prices (feat-018) — so accuracy is what ships. FIXTURE RE-LABEL: the feat-033 labels had been padded toward a ~9-per-type target, putting many LVN labels on high-volume bins (e.g. fixture-1's 30200 was in BOTH lists and is the POC); all 8 relabeled to genuine structure (HVN peaks; LVN troughs/taper-knees), then snapped to nearest real extrema. Tuned result (Config B, chosen for generalization over train-max to avoid holdout overfit): TRAIN LVN F1 0.46 / HVN F1 0.69 (gate PASS); HOLDOUT LVN 0.36 / HVN 0.61 (reported, never tuned against). HVN detection is solid; LVN localization is the known-hard part (architecture's #1 engine risk) and this is an honest first cut — improving it is future work (better taper algorithm / more fixtures). lib/engine/lvnDetection.test.ts: 10 synthetic mechanics tests (single-peak hill, double-distribution valley, flat profile, <3-bin guard, shoulder-noise robustness, taper-edge knee, no-plateau negative, descending-order + peakVolume, no-mutate, tuned-defaults). ./init.sh green: typecheck 0, lint 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings), 196 tests pass (19 files, +10), next build OK.

features.name: terrainZones.ts
features.description: Contiguous Stratosphere->Abyss zone stack with the No-Gap invariant (Price[N]===Price2[N+1]); classify regions by volume (acceptance/HVN vs rejection/LVN) cross-referenced with delta sign (absorption vs initiative). Engine assembles + validates borders. MGI-ANCHORED BORDER PROMOTION (doctrine: knowledge/doctrine/chart-reading.md 'Internal partitioning' + 'Valley+MGI=Trench, Shelf+MGI=Wall, Peak+MGI=Magnet'): a raw acceptance border (LVN valley/shelf) only becomes a HARD PARTITION when a major MGI level (from feat-012 mgiPriority) aligns with it. Anchor the classification on the MGI levels: for each major MGI, inspect the LOCAL volume profile and classify it — deep valley between two blocks -> Trench (Iron Trench); high-volume block dropping off sharply into a void with the MGI at the shelf edge -> Wall (Iron Ledge; overrides the bell-curve read — wVWAP at a block edge is a Wall, not a Magnet); MGI surrounded by thick roughly-equal volume with no distinct dip -> Magnet (invalidation — cannot be a structural border or a T3 Campaign Max). THIS IS THE HOME FOR HARD-LEDGE DETECTION: the standalone feat-014/035 LVN detector deliberately does NOT chase tall/shallow ledges (a whole-profile ledge scan is unseparable from ordinary distribution flanks by a threshold — investigated + rejected in feat-035, net-negative). Anchoring on the few MGI prices instead avoids that false-positive explosion, so the local shelf/valley test here should FAVOR RECALL: the MGI cross-reference can only PRUNE a spurious border, never CREATE a missing one, and detection is code-owned (feat-018: the LLM cannot add/adjust node prices), so a missed shelf-at-MGI is unrecoverable while an extra flagged shelf is cheap (dropped unless it happens to sit on an MGI). Consumes lvnDetection LVN/HVN output (feat-014) + Summary POC/VAH/VAL (feat-002) + MGI levels (feat-012). NOTE: the Magnet-side check overlaps feat-015 magnetCheck (POC/VAH/VAL/HVN vs MGI); keep the Magnet-Check logic single-sourced between the two (share a helper or have terrainZones consume magnetCheck's magnet classification rather than re-deriving it).

features.description: Bundle-data math review (2026-08-07, session following the Codex delta-intensity redundancy claim): prototype validation on two live bundles (2026-08-06 18:33 UTC, 630 bars; 16:26 UTC, 534 bars) found one order-flow construct with a real, replicated edge that the engine does not compute. An effort-vs-result absorption print is an exec bar where aggression was heavy but price refused to move: |delta| >= the 75th percentile of the series' |ask-bid| AND candle body <= 25% of the bar's high-low range. When such a bar prints after a directional move (>10 pts net over the prior 10 bars), price reversed within the next 10 bars 64%/71% of the time vs a 57% base rate, and the mean 10-bar move AGAINST the prior trend roughly doubled (+13.2/+15.9 pts vs +7.1/+7.9 baseline) — consistent across both bundles. This is Wyckoff effort-without-result made numeric, and it fills a real gap: stallConfirmation is level-anchored (needs a candidate border), while this detector is level-FREE — it fires anywhere on the tape, including at levels the briefing never mapped. Implementation: extend computeBarFlow (lib/engine/barFlow.ts) with an absorptionPrints reduction — count in the recent window, plus the most recent print's side (absorbing buys vs sells, from delta sign vs prior-move direction), price, and bars-ago — computed from existing ExecBar fields only (no new export columns); thresholds (P75 delta percentile, 25% body fraction, 10-pt/10-bar prior-move qualifier) as named exported constants for the doctrine drift guard. Surface via engineFacts into the analyze/update and eval prompts as raw facts (advisory context, not a gate), alongside the existing climax/divergence lines. The developing fact carries a maturity qualifier so the model knows how much to trust an unfinished value area -- elapsed RTH minutes and session volume so far against the time-of-day expectation from feat-094 -- plus range-used-so-far against the completed-session median (445 vs 464 pts on this bundle: nearly a full day's travel already printed). Must degrade cleanly: pre-open and overnight bundles have no in-progress row at all, so detect by date, never by position, and null the fact when absent. features.name: Price impact per unit of order flow (Kyle's lambda)
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 B3 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): regress per-bar (close-open) on per-bar delta over a rolling window. Lambda is the quantitative statement of absorption -- low lambda means aggressive flow is being met without price moving, high lambda means the book is thin and small flow travels far. Measured on bundle 1c15934a: whole-session lambda 83.7 pts per 1000 net delta (R^2 0.27); rolling 30-bar min 18.2 / median 76.4 / max 155.0, a 9x spread, with the lowest-lambda windows (08:23, 09:20, 08:03) reading as absorption and the highest (06:29, 01:13, 09:57) as vacuum. Honest caveat to carry into the implementation: per-window R^2 runs 0.02-0.44, so lambda is a noisy estimate and the fact MUST carry a confidence gate -- report only when R^2 and window volume clear a threshold, else null, following the degradation pattern the other engine facts already use. The signal is the CHANGE in lambda, not its level. Generalises the current absorption scan, which can only see stacks that happen to fall inside the ~25-bin delta profiles; lambda works everywhere price has traded. Relationship to feat-089: that feature's effort-vs-result absorption PRINT is the same idea as a binary per-bar test (heavy |delta|, small body); lambda is its continuous, windowed form. Ship feat-087 first -- it has replicated base-rate-controlled evidence and this does not -- then use lambda for the regime read the print cannot give. PRIOR NEGATIVE RESULT (2026-08-07 delta-intensity review, branch claude/delta-intensity-redundancy-xe1bbj): lambda was tested AS A TIMING FILTER and rejected -- 60 percent vs a 58 percent base rate, i.e. near-nil. That does not refute this feature, which scopes lambda as a continuous liquidity/absorption REGIME read feeding the narrative and gating other signals, not as a trigger; but it does mean lambda must clear its own base-rate control in that framing before it ships, and it sits below feat-087 and feat-094 in priority until it does.
